chapter: England, later career and closing thoughts
title: Foreign offers, the cost of touring and working by feeling
summary: She would tour Europe again only with records out, prefers her own sympathetic musicians such as Morris Edwards and George Duvivier, and plays by feeling.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I got a letter just a few weeks ago from somebody wanting to get -- bring me -- from a Scandinavian booking agent. And I've gotten calls within the last year from people wanting me to go into Europe, you know. But my feeling now is that I would like to do something like that, if I have something going, some records going, you know, if the records were resurrected or reissued or something. But I think just to go someplace now just to be going, in the first place you've got to dicker and you've got to talk about money and the kind of money that you should get now, because you can't afford to go -- I can't, and I speak for myself, and I'm sure I'm speaking for many other people -- it's too expensive now to attempt to go. And when I travel I use my own musicians with me. Not that I put any other musicians down. Unless I'm fortunate enough to go in a town, like when I go to New York, I have musicians there that have worked with me. Morris Edwards, for instance, who is a very fine bass player. Well, Morris Edwards worked with me out here in California before he even went to New York to live. He works with me. And of course, as I mentioned, George Duvivier, who's so busy now he doesn't have time to work with anybody, any one person too long, you know. He's so much in demand.

So, if I'm fortunate enough to do that, but when you are doing a certain type of thing and you feel a certain type of rhythm, that I do, because I feel that what I'm doing, it's a sensitive -- I feel every movement that I make. I work really by my feeling, you know. When I play, that's the way I play the piano. I work strictly by feeling. And every musician -- any musician -- I don't say every -- but every musician who comes along doesn't feel this, you see. So there are certain people that I enjoy working with because I know they sense what I'm doing. They're sensitive to what I'm doing, and this makes me a better performer, when I work with people who really understand what I'm doing and who really feel what I'm doing. I don't want to work for somebody who's just, 'Well, I'm working with Nellie and I'm going to get some money.'
You know what I mean, 'I'm going to get some money for doing this,' and so on. So that doesn't --
